pr_body:
Throw an error, with duplicate enum names as possible reason), if the PostgresQueryRunner::getEnumTypeName result is undefined. Possible "fix"  for https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/issues/7084 (at least the error message should help the user)

### Description of change

Throw an error if PostgresQueryRunner::getEnumTypeName result is undefined. This error message contains
a hint for the developer what could be a possible reason why the `result` is `undefined`.

This helps if the user encounters #7084.

issue_context.title: Postgres: duplicate enum names lead to a unhelpful error message during migration generation
issue_context.body:
<!--

  on the best places to ask questions!

  https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/support.md
-->

## Issue Description

If you accidentally create two enums with the same name, the error thrown during `typeorm migration:generate -n`  return the following unhelpful error:
 ```
Error during migration generation:
TypeError: Cannot read property 'udt_schema' of undefined
    at PostgresQueryRunner.<anonymous> (/home/user/project/src/driver/postgres/PostgresQueryRunner.ts:2023:38)
    at step (/home/user/project/node_modules/tslib/tslib.js:139:27)
    at Object.next (/home/user/project/node_modules/tslib/tslib.js:120:57)
    at fulfilled (/home/user/project/node_modules/tslib/tslib.js:110:62)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:94:5)
```

### Expected Behavior
 ```
Error during migration generation:
Duplicate enum name: nameOfEnum
```

### Actual Behavior
Unhelpful error
 ```
Error during migration generation:
TypeError: Cannot read property 'udt_schema' of undefined
    at PostgresQueryRunner.<anonymous> (/home/user/project/src/driver/postgres/PostgresQueryRunner.ts:2023:38)
    at step (/home/user/project/node_modules/tslib/tslib.js:139:27)
    at Object.next (/home/user/project/node_modules/tslib/tslib.js:120:57)
    at fulfilled (/home/user/project/node_modules/tslib/tslib.js:110:62)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:94:5)
```
### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create enum1
2. Create enum2.
3. Create enitity
4. Add Column enum1 with name `Enum1`
5. Add Column enum2 with name `Enum2`
6. Run `typeorm migration:generate -n`

```typescript
enum Enum1 {
    test = "test"
}

enum Enum2 {
    test = "test"
}

@Entity("test")
export class Test {
    @PrimaryGeneratedColumn({
        name: "id",
        type: "int",
        unsigned: true,
    })
    public id!: number;

    @Column("enum", {
        enum: Enum1,
        name: "enum1",
        nullable: false,
    })
    public provider!: Enum1;

    @Column("enum", {
        enum: Enum2,
        name: "enum1",
        nullable: false,
    })
    public method!: Enum2;
}
```

comments: Really this should be detected as a duplicate column in general? The postgres error is essentially just a side effect - does it also happen with two non-enum columns?

> Really this should be detected as a duplicate column in general?
Imo it should be detected and a detailed error should be printed.

> does it also happen with two non-enum columns
Did not try that one, but I guess this specific error only happens with enums because the error happens in `getEnumTypeName` method.

> Imo it should be detected and a detailed error should be printed.

Agreed, I will take a look at this later.

review_comments: Strange that it would end up being `undefined`, the query would surely be identical between the two columns if name is the same?

Have you tried to reproduce it?

That's the behavior I encountered.

Imo you should think about using typescripts `--noUncheckedIndexedAccess`.
